comment: Rules of the new game (ADR 0028, docs/projekt-gry.md). Time: 10 ticks a second; rates are per minute of play. Amounts are whole units (two decimals allowed). density: how many times more hexes than the legacy map of the same size (a hex is room for one building). economyEveryTicks, populationEveryTicks: rhythms of docs/wydajnosc.md. Start: the stock and people of a new tribe. Food: every person eats foodPerPersonPerMinute, paid once a minute at the ration (see rations); people told to gather pick up food, wood and stone around their settlement (forage). Growth: a fed settlement below its housing grows growthPercentPerMinute of its people a minute (at least minGrowthPerMinute); it does not grow while it has no food, nor while its food falls and less than stopBelowRations rations are left (Patryk, 2026-11-22: variant C; deaths from hunger come at the rations; starvePercentPerMinute is not used). resumeCostPercent: resuming a paused construction costs this much of the building's price again. Settlement levels: radius in hexes of the territory, housing and storage given by the settlement itself, the price of the upgrade. Buildings: workers (jobs), price, buildSeconds, terrain rules (biomes, relief, needsWater = next to a lake, sea or river, deposit = a surface deposit on the hex, minFertility), production per worker per minute, deposit bonus in percent, housing and storage they add. bonusRelief and bonusReliefPercent: extra production on hills or mountains. Storage: goods lie in the settlement where they were made; every finished building adds buildingStorage of room for each good unless it gives its own storage (storehouses). Construction materials are carried by porters from the nearest storehouse (or the settlement centre); the work goes as far as the delivered materials allow. groups: tags that technology effects can aim at (e.g. melee, tools).

foundSettlement.comment: Settlers found a camp at least minDistance hexes from every other settlement centre, on land nobody owns; their people live there.

terrainCost.comment: Walking cost of a hex in percent of a flat open hex.

research.comment: A technology needs experience in the technologies before it (worker-minutes in their buildings), then its price in goods and its time. It is cheaper by neighbourDiscountPercent for every known people that knows it (at most maxNeighbourDiscountPercent). One research at a time. maxSupportPercent: schools and academies speed a branch of research at most this much. pace: percent of the price, of the experience and goods made asked for, and of the time of the technologies of each era (index = era).

technologies.name: Foraging
technologies.gives: Gatherers' huts and woodcutters; the people of a settlement can gather food, wood and stone around it.

technologies.name: Dwellings
technologies.gives: Huts.

technologies.name: Stockpiling
technologies.gives: Storehouses.

technologies.name: Carrying
technologies.gives: Baskets: porters carry 20 instead of 5; tracks.

technologies.name: Scouting
technologies.gives: Scouts.

technologies.name: Migration
technologies.gives: Settlers.

technologies.name: Fire
technologies.gives: Hearths; gatherers +10%.

technologies.name: Stone tools
technologies.gives: Quarries, toolmakers.

technologies.name: Hunting
technologies.gives: Hunters' lodges; hunters with spears and slings.

technologies.name: Shelters
technologies.gives: Huts give 2 more homes; clay pits.

technologies.name: Herbal lore
technologies.gives: Herbalists: hunters near them +25%, the wounded heal; growth a little faster; epidemics 15% milder.

technologies.name: Sewing
technologies.gives: Tailors: clothing makes workers faster, most of all in winter.

technologies.name: Flint weapons
technologies.gives: Warriors with wooden spears, clubs and slings.

technologies.name: Agriculture
technologies.gives: Farms (the more fertile the land, the more they give); camps can become villages.

technologies.name: Pottery
technologies.gives: Potters (pottery, used in many later things), granaries.

technologies.name: Animal husbandry
technologies.gives: Pastures (twice as good on cattle).

technologies.name: Masonry
technologies.gives: Stone houses (more homes, warmer in winter); masons (quarries near them dig more); bridges where roads cross rivers.

technologies.name: Weaving
technologies.gives: Weavers (textiles).

technologies.name: Irrigation
technologies.gives: Irrigation ditches drawn from water (at most 4 hexes): farms on watered hexes +25%; droughts 40% milder.

technologies.name: Barter
technologies.gives: Trading posts; trade with other civilizations (one agreement per trading post).

technologies.name: Palisade
technologies.gives: Palisades drawn on hexes: they wound enemies attacking through them.

technologies.name: Prospecting
technologies.gives: Ore signs: circles on seen land where an ore of our era lies; prospectors can search them one by one. New signs with each era: copper, then tin, gold and silver, iron ore, saltpeter.

technologies.name: Copper working
technologies.gives: Copper mines.

technologies.name: Fishing
technologies.gives: Fishing huts by rivers and the sea.

technologies.name: Rafts
technologies.gives: Raft landings: our people cross the river next to them.

technologies.name: Polished stone tools
technologies.gives: Quarries, woodcutters, clay pits +15%.

technologies.name: Hide shields
technologies.gives: Warriors and residents +15%.

technologies.name: Hafted weapons
technologies.gives: Warriors and residents +20%.

technologies.name: Bronze working
technologies.gives: Tin mines, bronze smiths, charcoal burners (charcoal from wood: the fuel of smiths).

technologies.name: Bronze weapons
technologies.gives: Armourers (arms), spearmen.

technologies.name: The wheel
technologies.gives: With Horseback riding: caravans (they take horses). Porters and caravans 50% faster.

technologies.name: Writing
technologies.gives: Schools: every worker speeds one branch of research we choose (+15%).

technologies.name: Horseback riding
technologies.gives: Stables (horses, at most 32 each), horsemen.

technologies.name: Sailing
technologies.gives: Harbours; transport ships (carry armies) and trade ships (carry goods).

technologies.name: Currency
technologies.gives: Mints (coins from copper); pay and be paid in coins; research −5%.

technologies.name: Code of laws
technologies.gives: A town office: with Masonry, villages can become towns.

technologies.name: Archery
technologies.gives: Bows: hunters become archers (stronger, longer reach).

technologies.name: Barracks
technologies.gives: Barracks: soldiers wait there between wars; training twice as fast.

technologies.name: Stone walls
technologies.gives: Stone walls drawn on hexes: enemies cannot pass until they break them.

technologies.name: Bronze age arms
technologies.gives: Better weapons and armour: melee +30%, infantry +20%.

technologies.name: Bronze tools
technologies.gives: Quarries, woodcutters, mines +20%.

technologies.name: Iron working
technologies.gives: Iron mines, blacksmiths (tools from iron).

technologies.name: Iron weapons
technologies.gives: Weaponsmiths (arms from iron), swordsmen.

technologies.name: Mathematics
technologies.gives: Builders' yards: their workers make building in their settlement up to 30% faster.

technologies.name: Construction
technologies.gives: Great storehouses; with Civil service, towns can become cities. Stone houses: +4 homes (they grow a storey).

technologies.name: Civil service
technologies.gives: Province offices; provinces; a larger reach of the administration; with Construction, towns can become cities.

technologies.name: Roads
technologies.gives: Paved roads: much faster than tracks, also over hills; major trade routes.

technologies.name: Engineering
technologies.gives: Siege workshops (their workers build engines faster), catapults; aqueducts drawn from water to towns. Stone houses: +4 homes (they grow a storey).

technologies.name: Medicine
technologies.gives: Bathhouses: in their settlement epidemics are milder and people grow faster.

technologies.name: Philosophy
technologies.gives: Academies (every worker speeds one branch of research, +20%); rarer thinkers and advisors.

technologies.name: Shipbuilding
technologies.gives: Shipyards, warships (fight at sea, carry armies); larger trade ships.

technologies.name: Brick making
technologies.gives: Brickworks (bricks from clay and charcoal): iron-age buildings and cities are built of bricks.

technologies.name: Shepherding
technologies.gives: Sheepfolds (wool) and cloth weavers (cloth and better clothing from wool); weavers can become cloth weavers.

technologies.name: Iron age arms
technologies.gives: Better weapons and armour: melee +30%, infantry and cavalry +25%.

technologies.name: Iron tools
technologies.gives: Quarries, woodcutters, mines +25%; farms +15%.

technologies.name: Feudalism
technologies.gives: Manors; a larger reach of the administration.

technologies.name: Chivalry
technologies.gives: Knights (they take horses).

technologies.name: Steel
technologies.gives: Steelworks.

technologies.name: Castles
technologies.gives: Castles (+220% defence).

technologies.name: Heavy plough
technologies.gives: Farms also on poorer land; farms +15%.

technologies.name: Crossbows
technologies.gives: Crossbowmen.

technologies.name: Guilds
technologies.gives: Guild halls: workshops in their settlement +25% while they work. Stone houses: +8 homes (they grow a storey).

technologies.name: Mills
technologies.gives: Mills by rivers: farms in their settlement +20% while they work.

technologies.name: University
technologies.gives: Universities (every worker speeds one branch of research, +25%).

technologies.name: Medieval arms
technologies.gives: Steel weapons and plate armour: melee, infantry and cavalry +30%.

technologies.name: Crop rotation
technologies.gives: Farms +25%.

technologies.name: Longbow
technologies.gives: Archers and crossbowmen +30%.

technologies.name: Sawmills
technologies.gives: Sawmills by rivers (planks from wood): medieval buildings are built of planks.

technologies.name: Lime mortar
technologies.gives: Lime kilns (mortar from stone and charcoal): castles, manors and universities need mortar.

technologies.name: Trebuchet
technologies.gives: Siege engines +100% against settlements.

thinkers.comment: A people has one thinker. Rarity sets how much cheaper (costPercent) and how much less experience (experiencePercent) research needs; some take less experience but cost more. A thinker retires after retireMinutes; the successor (II, III…) keeps the school but each generation loses generationLossPercent of the edge. A new candidate shows up every offerMinutes; hiring costs hirePrice times the rarity's priceTimes.

advisors.comment: A people has at most one advisor. A candidate shows up every offerMinutes with one or two fields (economy, growth, research, expansion); hiring costs hirePrice times the rarity's priceTimes, and the advisor eats upkeepFoodPerMinute. The advisor gives one piece of advice at a time, only in its fields.

war.comment: Units fight once a second (combatEveryTicks). A side deals people × strength × (100 + terrain bonus + upgrades) / 100 × luck (lowLuckPercent..highLuckPercent) hundredths of a person, killed on the other side. Melee reaches the next hex, ranged units their range. A settlement under attack defends with defenderPercent of its people at defenderStrength each, raised by its finished fortifications; at captureBelowPeople it is taken. Soldiers are fed by rations (see rations). Attacking a people without a declared war is a surprise attack: the victim and everyone who met both remember it (reputation). declareReputation: reputation every declaration of war costs. tributeNeedsKills: people a people must have lost to the war before its AI agrees to pay tribute. tributeFoodMaxPercent: most food (percent of the payer's) a tribute takes. maxWars: most wars a people may be in at once (design chapter 8); nobody may declare war on a people already in that many. The war score counts from the start of the current war; tributeAfterSeconds: peace with tribute only this long after the war began. reputationFloor: reputation never falls below it; badReputation: below it the AI declares new wars half as often. reputationRegenPerMinute: a bad name heals by this much a minute (up to 0) while the people is not the aggressor of a war going on.

events.comment: Every people draws one event from the shared pool every everyMinutes (a random minute within the spread), never one another people has right now. An event lasts its seconds. productionPercent changes the production of the listed goods, eatPercent what people eat, losePercentPerMinute kills that share of people a minute, destroyBuilding burns one random finished building at the start. field: the advisor field that gives advice on it.

pool.name: Drought
pool.advice: Drought: build fishing huts or stop growing for a while; the stores must last.

pool.name: Hard winter
pool.advice: A hard winter: people eat more. Keep food stores high and do not train settlers now.

pool.name: Epidemic
pool.advice: Sickness spreads: the fewer people we move around, the better; wait it out.

pool.name: Fire
pool.advice: A fire took a building: rebuild what we need most first.

pool.name: Flood
pool.advice: The rivers flood: fields and clay pits work at half. Use the stores.

diplomacy.comment: Peoples consider a treaty only when they have known each other for knownMinutes, their settlements are at most borderHexes apart, they have not fought for peaceMinutes and the other's reputation is above minReputation; then a trade agreement when they lack a good the other makes or the other knows more technologies, an alliance when they share an enemy. At most one offer to the same people every offerCooldownMinutes, refusalCooldownMinutes after a refusal. Trade agreements need the barter technology. Barter goods travel in caravans; the AI takes a barter worth acceptWorthPercent of what it gives (100 with currency) and keeps twice what it gives.

roads.comment: Levels of roads. walkPercent: walking cost on them, of the hex's cost (capped at 150 so roads cross rough land). reach: hexes from our nearest settlement. supply: goods carriers bring to a new camp joined to our roads.

seasons.comment: Winter comes every cycleMinutes and lasts winterMinutes (no years: playability first). Work is rounded down to steps of workStepPermille. In winter every worker works at winterWorkPercent; buildings with winterPercent lose that much more (gathering and fields). Peoples are told warnSeconds before.

clothing.comment: Every set of clothing a worker has adds bonusPercent. Outside winter only the first set counts (at most 100+bonus); in winter more sets count, up to winterMaxPercent. Worked out per settlement: sets = clothing in store / people. Sets wear out: wearPerPersonPerMinute.

forage.comment: People of a settlement told to gather pick up food, wood and stone around it. Per gatherer per minute at richness 100: perMinute. A hex's richness: food and wood by biome, stone by relief; deposits and rivers add. A settlement's richness is the mean over the land hexes in its radius (worked out when it is founded or grows). subsistencePercent: idle gatherers always find at least this share of the food they eat (any land, any season), so a people left alone survives but gathers no surplus.

rivers.comment: Until freeFromEra, rivers can be crossed only next to one's own building that gives a crossing (raft landings).

works.comment: Works drawn on hexes; price and seconds per hex. ditch: farms on watered hexes +farmPercent. palisade: enemies at war standing on it lose woundPercentPerSecond of their people a second. wall: foreign units cannot enter until its strength (hundredths of damage) is broken. aqueduct: a settlement it reaches grows growthBonus% a minute faster and suffers resistEpidemicPercent less from epidemics.

trees.comment: Groves on open land, in clumps: groveChance percent of a biome's land hexes. A grove gives groveWoodPercent of a forest's wood to woodcutters and gatherers.

rations.comment: Every everySeconds a settlement feeds everyone it has: its residents and its units (soldiers, scouts, carriers, settlers on the way), each eating food.foodPerPersonPerMinute for the time since the last ration. Short of food, its units are fed first (fighting ones first), then its workers, then the people without a job: those go hungry first. Hungry people work, gather, fight and walk at hungryPercent. Missed again at the next ration: starvingPercent, and starveLosePercent of the hungry (at least 1) die then and at every further missed ration. One full ration ends it.

startPhase.comment: pickSeconds: time a player has to choose. blockRadius: hexes around a taken start where no other people may start. blockFuzz: the shown circle is centred up to this many hexes from the real start and is this much wider, so it hides the start. scoreRadius, roomRadius: hexes looked at when scoring a start (its own land, the room around). neighbourMaxHexes: every people starts on the main continent (the largest land) and, after the first, at most this many hexes by land from a people already placed (while choosing: from the shown circles); 0 = anywhere. neighbourMinHexes: placed starts and the AI's choices keep this far from other starts when the land allows (room to grow).

survey.comment: What is known of the land (Patryk, 2026-11-19). On our own land everything is known. Beyond it, seeing a hex shows only the surface deposits; the rest is found by units that survey (units[].survey): standing still, they look at every hex within radius. rock: prospectors find stone, clay, flint and ores, each ore only from the era in eras (a people recognises an ore once it is in the era of the technology that works it, even before it knows the technology); ores not listed are never found in these eras. soil: surveyors find fertility and the deposits in soil.

combat.comment: Battle in steps of stepTicks. A unit fights every enemy unit next to it (ranged: within range, only while standing). Per step it kills engaged people x strength x weapon / armour of the target x terrain x flank x charge x bonus against the target's kind x fed x luck / killDivisor. Engaged people: at most frontPerContact for each enemy it touches. weapon and armour: multipliers for levels 0-4 (armourVsRangedBonus: armour counts this much more against arrows). Flank: damage taken by how many enemy units touch the target (index = count, last for more). Terrain: per level of relief higher than the target (flat 0, hills 1, mountains 2) reliefPercent, at most reliefMaxPercent; per elevationStep of height above it elevationPercent, at most elevationMaxPercent. Cover of the target's hex (forest or grove, palisade or wall) against ranged and melee, lost when enemies touch it from opposite sides. Attacking across a river without a bridge: riverPercent. Roads and swamps: openPercent more taken. Leaving enemies: each enemy next to it strikes once, disengagePercent of a step (cavalry cavalryDisengagePercent), unless another unit of ours stays next to that enemy. Charge: cavalry that walked chargeHexes or more before contact strikes chargePercent once (not against units that stop charges). One army unit to a hex: a unit that stops on another steps aside. Zone of control: a unit stops when it comes next to an enemy, and from there goes on only one hex at a time. Weapons only (shock): no armour, shockTrainPercent of the time. Single player: a battle after calmSeconds of calm slows time to x1. A unit falling to warnPercents of its full size is told in the chronicle. A unit with no way to its target searches again after chaseRetrySeconds and gives it up after chaseGiveUp failures.

eraGateways.comment: Era key: technology of that era that must be known (besides eraAdvanceTechs of it) to enter the next era.

ruins.comment: A settlement empty for emptySeconds (not the last of its people) becomes a ruin: its land is nobody's, its buildings stand ruined. Settlers on or next to its centre take it: the land is claimed again and every ruined building is a site that needs rebuildPercent of its price. razedKeepPercent: of a razed settlement's store this percent stays in the ruins, the rest is lost.

siege.comment: An enemy army unit at war within blockadeRange of a settlement's centre blockades it: it works at blockadeWorkPercent, trains no units, starts no buildings and sends or takes no caravans; the blockade lifts liftSeconds after the last such unit leaves. Defenders: the settlement's own army units standing on its land (they take damage divided by its defence), its guard and its residents. Guard: a standing garrison from its works and buildings, guardPerPalisadeHexPercent / guardPerWallHexPercent hundredths of a man per palisade or wall hex of its land, plus each building's guard (a castle); it grows back guardRegrowPerMinute a minute when not blockaded and costs nothing. Guard strikes with guardStrength, residents with war.defenderStrength, times the settlement's defence. Attackers' blows fall on the guard first, then on the fighting residents (war.defenderPercent of the residents when the blockade began); residents never fall below residentsFloorPercent of that number by fighting; the rest are defenceless. With no guard, no defending units and no fighting residents left the settlement falls: its taker chooses within choiceSeconds (else it is taken): take it, sack it (sackPercent of each good goes by caravan to the taker's nearest settlement, and can be raided on the way; nobody may besiege it again for sackImmuneSeconds) or raze it (a ruin; its residents flee to their people's nearest settlement). assaultAfterSeconds: the attackers strike the guard and residents only this long after the blockade began (time for the defender to react). aiTakeWithinHexes: the AI takes a fallen settlement this close to its own and sacks one farther away.

supply.comment: An army unit on its people's land or within rangeHexes of it is fed at the ration by its home settlement and fills its provisions: food for carryMinutes minutes of its people. Farther away it eats its provisions; before them the land gives what landHands foragers would gather on its hex (forage.perMinute food at the hex's richness, times landPercent): a small unit lives off the land longer than a big one. With no provisions left it goes hungry, then starves. A caravan can carry food to a unit in the field (it follows the unit, and can be raided on the way). noWaySeconds: a caravan to a unit there is no way to is refused, and the AI sends none to that unit for this long.

armyLimit.comment: Army units (not people) a people may have: perLevel for each settlement by its level (camp, village, town, city), plus perBuilding for each finished building of those kinds, plus perTech for each of those technologies known. Training stops at the limit; a big army stays possible, but costs food at every ration.

veterans.comment: Experience belongs to a kind of unit, not to a unit: every enemy its units kill adds one to that kind's experience. At each of the levels (kills in all) the people picks one of the options for that kind, for all its units of that kind, now and later: strengthPercent more damage, takenPercent of the damage taken (negative = less), speedPercent faster walking. Options stack. shareNearHexes: an enemy killed counts for every kind of ours fighting within this many hexes of it, once per kind.

upgradeCaravans.comment: A settlement short of the goods for its upgrade gets them by caravan from our other settlements: they carry what is missing plus extraPercent of the price of that good (at least 1), as far as the senders have it. When they arrive short, the AI asks again only after aiRetrySeconds.

eraEntryMade.comment: Era key: goods the people must have made (in all) to enter that era, besides its techs and gateway.

alerts.comment: foodLowMinutes: a settlement that eats more than it makes is warned when its food lasts this long or less. noResearchSeconds: the reminder that nothing is being researched comes only this long after the last research ended (or the game began), and only when something can be researched.

ai.comment: homesFoodMinutes: the AI builds new homes only while its food lasts this many minutes of eating. smallPeople: below this many people the AI trains no units but settlers and builds no new workplace while jobs are free. peacefulStartMinutes: the AI declares no war in the first this many minutes of a game. foodMarginPercent: outside winter the AI wants food made to exceed its eating by this percent (the summer surplus has to cover the winter); short of it, it builds food and no new homes. foodSitesPerPeople: one more food building may be under construction at a time per this many people. inputRouteTripMinutes: a workshop whose settlement uses more of an input than it makes gets a standing route from our settlement with the most to spare of it, carrying this many minutes of the use a trip while the target holds less than inputRouteTargetMinutes of it; the source keeps inputRouteKeepMinutes of its own use. At most inputRoutesPerSettlement such routes per settlement we have. inputMakerStoreMinutes: when its workshops use more of an input than the people makes, the AI builds another maker of it (one at a time) until the store lasts this many minutes of the shortfall. starvedProspectors: while our workshops use more of an ore (iron, copper...) than we make and no deposit of it we know is free for a mine, the AI keeps up to this many prospectors (else one) and sends them farther. thinkEveryTicks: ticks between two thoughts of one AI people. wayToMinutes: the AI remembers this long (plus up to a minute, different for each target) whether its armies can reach a settlement; one thought searches one way at most. careSettlementPeople: people a settlement needs before the AI builds there a school, bathhouse, academy or university. researchKeepFoodMinutes: the AI starts a research only when this many minutes of its eating stay in store after paying.

amounts.comment: Whole units the AI decides by. lowFood: below it the AI builds food first. lowGood: a good it uses below this (and not made) is short: it builds a maker or asks for a trade. lowTools: builds a toolmaker below it. foodSourceKeep: a settlement sending food keeps at least this. foodSendAtLeast: a caravan of food carries at least this. shareLow: a workshop's input below this calls a caravan from the richest settlement, which keeps shareKeep plus shareMargin; a caravan carries shareTrip. routeSourceLow: an input route whose source falls below this (and makes none) ends; a route trip carries at least this. unitSupplyHomeKeep: a home settlement supplies its unit only while keeping this much food beyond twice the load. warNetFood: no new soldiers while food made a minute exceeds eating by less than this.

aiBattle.comment: retreatInjuredPercent: a unit at war with this share of its people wounded goes home to heal; retreatSizePercent: one with fewer people than this share of its size goes home and guards it. engageHexes: a seen enemy army this close to a soldier is fought first, by every soldier this close to it (a flank). An offensive starts from our settlement nearest the target: soldiers within musterFromHexes but farther than musterHexes gather there in formation, and the march starts once musterPercent of the power stands there.

lodes.comment: sizes: every deposit is small, medium or large (a mine or a bonus on it gives percent of the usual), drawn by weight; inside a region of its kind by regionWeight. regional: these deposits gather in regions: `regions` centres per 10000 land hexes, each `regionHexes` around; outside them only outsideKeepPercent of the deposits stay, and as many are added inside. signs: Prospecting shows, for each ore of the people's era (eras), up to perOre circles of signRadius hexes on land the people has seen within reachHexes of its settlements; the ore lies in the circle, its centre is moved up to offsetHexes away. Signs are worked out every recountSeconds.

peace.comment: Peace offers name goods and amounts, maybe one settlement, and a length of peace (minutes: one of these). Only the side the war favours may demand; the other may offer a white peace or give something. A settlement may be demanded unless it is the people's first; our army must besiege it or it must lie within settlementHexes of our land. Worth: goods at their worth, a settlement at settlementWorthPerPerson food per person plus settlementBuildingPercent of the price of its finished buildings. What the course of the war asks of the loser: one percent of its wealth (goods and settlements but its first) per scorePerPercent points of war score lead plus one per wearinessPerPercent points of weariness lead, at most maxPercent; a loser who declared the war gives aggressorExtraPercent more. The AI takes terms within that, with up to aiGiveMarginPercent more give the more peaceful it is; the margin changes by aiLosingLengthPercent (when it loses) or aiWinningLengthPercent (when it wins) for each length. breakPercent: reputation for breaking a peace of each length, percent of a surprise attack's. whiteTruceMinutes: after a white peace neither side may declare war on the other (or attack it) for this many minutes.

weariness.comment: War weariness of a people in each of its wars, 0-100: perMinute a minute of war, perLostPercent for each percent of its people the enemy killed, hungerPerMinute a minute while a settlement of it is hungry, besiegedPerMinute a minute for each settlement the enemy besieges, sacked, taken (also razed) and caravanRaided at once; it falls by peaceFallPerMinute a minute in peace. From workFrom up, buildings that use goods work less, down to workMaxLossPercent less at 100 (the highest weariness of its wars counts). The AI looks for peace from aiPeaceAt, and a losing AI offers goods from aiPayAt.

march.comment: Soldiers sent at the same goal share a way: a soldier within shareHexes of where the last search for that goal started, less than shareSeconds ago, walks there (a search of at most joinSearch hexes) and then the same way. One long search per expedition instead of one per soldier.

aiWar.comment: When the AI starts a war (Patryk, 2026-11-23). It never breaks a peace that still runs. A target settlement not seen for intelMinutes gets a scout first. It attacks when its power is powerTimes the defence it knows, the settlement holds at least gainPercent of the soldiers it sends in people (the gain), and the target people is not small: a people whose known people is below smallTargetPercent of ours, or below smallTargetPeople, is spared unless its reputation is below war.badReputation. Only an AI with aggression of at least surpriseAggression attacks without declaring war. While a people it met has a bad name, the AI keeps fearArmyPercent more soldiers and seeks defensive alliances against it. At war it offers peace when the enemy's score is losingScoreMargin above its own, when weary, or with randomPeacePercent chance a thought.

vision.comment: settlementSightBeyond: hexes a settlement sees beyond its own land. Units of a people we have not met that our settlements see, and whose people has seen the settlement, raise the alert 'Strangers' (not who nor where).

stores.comment: A good is full from fullPercent of the room until it falls below stillFullPercent; empty below 1 until it reaches stillEmptyBelow (whole units).

drawnPaths.comment: A path given to a unit, a patrol, a road or a work: at most maxHexes hexes in all, at most maxJumps points that do not touch the one before (the way between them is searched, at most jumpSearchNodes hexes each).

multiplayer.comment: nicknameSuffixes: a player whose nickname is already taken in a game gets one of these at random, one no other player there has (e.g. "Ania the Late").
